instrument: test/tool-handlers.test.ts harness: drive draft_reminder and send_reminder on the seed's draft LB-2026-0055 and on void LB-2026-0009; expect { ok: false } refusals naming draft and void, and no reminders row
title: draft_reminder and send_reminder chase a draft invoice nobody was billed for
body:
## Summary
`draft_reminder` writes, and the GATED `send_reminder` sends, a payment reminder for the seed's draft invoice LB-2026-0055 ($73,100), which the books count as billed to nobody; a void invoice is refused as "settled".

## Description
`draftReminderAction` (examples/ledgerbox/app/actions.ts:314) refuses only a zero balance (`:319`) and a dispute (`:321`). A draft has state `draft`, a positive balance and `days_overdue` 0 (lib/db.ts toRow), so it passes; `sendReminderAction` (`:375`) then sends whatever draft exists. Every other reading of the books already treats a draft as unissued: `COUNTED_OUT` (lib/db.ts) leaves it out of every total, `takesCredit` offers it no credit, `needsDecision` (components/lanes/model/attention.ts:54) and `statusOf` call it quiet. A void invoice is refused with "LB-2026-0009 is settled - nothing to chase." because its balance is forced to 0 - a reason that is not this one. This is the sibling of the domain-lib card "mark_paid and match_bank_line apply money to a draft nobody owes": same predicate, two more acts, one of them the act that reaches a person. Fixed looks like: both acts refuse `draft` and `void` with their own sentence, from one shared "is this invoice issued" predicate.

## Flow
- agent calls draft_reminder({ id: "LB-2026-0055", tone: "gentle" }) -> draftReminderAction -> passes both guards -> INSERT INTO reminders -> "Drafted a gentle reminder for elin.voss@tideline-press.example. Nothing has been sent."
- agent calls send_reminder({ id: "LB-2026-0055" }) -> host gates it -> person approves a card about an invoice never sent -> "Sent to Tideline Press <...>. This one cannot be taken back."
- draft_reminder on void LB-2026-0009 -> "is settled - nothing to chase."
- fix: one predicate in app/actions.ts beside the dispute guard; refusal sentences "LB-... is a draft - issue it before chasing" / "LB-... is void"

## Expected impact
A person approving a chase card would no longer be asked to send a dunning letter for an invoice the client never received; measured as 0 reminders for draft/void invoices on the seed. Could break: nothing in the demo journey chases a draft.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a reminder is only drafted or sent for an issued invoice that is owed
Before: probe through the tool harness on the seed: draft_reminder on LB-2026-0055 ok true, send_reminder ok true ("Sent to Tideline Press"); void answered "is settled"
After: predicted 2 of 2 refused with their own reasons (not built: the fix is app/actions.ts, ledgerbox-app-shell's file)
Method: probe - Before reproduced through BooksTools' real handlers; After needs the fix in a file outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

instrument: tools.test.ts: assert every manifest parameter whose handler checks a closed list carries that list as its enum (search_invoices.area vs CATEGORIES); seed by removing the enum
title: search_invoices takes its area as a free string where CATEGORIES is closed
body:
## Summary
`search_invoices.area` is published as a bare string although the six areas are a closed set (`CATEGORIES`); the model learns the vocabulary only by being refused.

## Description
lib/manifest.ts:97 declares `{ name: "area", type: "string", required: false }` with no enum, while the handler (examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/tools/search.ts:323) filters lanes by id and answers "No area called X" with the list. The lanes ARE `CATEGORIES` (lib/constants.ts), and the manifest's own header says "Enums are mandatory for anything that addresses UI" (lib/manifest.ts:37); `categorize.category` already carries `enum: CATEGORIES`. mcp-tools/tool-schema-design: "Enums over free strings wherever a closed set exists - the schema then teaches the legal vocabulary at selection time and the validator rejects the rest, one definition serving both readers." Fixed: `enum: [...CATEGORIES, "all"]` on the parameter (the handler treats "all" as no filter), so the door refuses a wrong area before the handler and the model sees the six names in the schema.

## Flow
- agent calls search_invoices({ area: "Design" }) (the label, not the id) -> passes the door (any string) -> search.ts finds no lane -> { ok: false, error: "No area called Design.", areas: [...] } -> a second call
- fix: lib/manifest.ts adds the enum; tools.test.ts's "bounded" test asserts it

## Expected impact
A model composing a search sees the six area ids before its first call; one wasted round trip per mislabelled area avoided. Could break: a caller sending a label instead of an id is refused at the door instead of by the handler (same information, earlier).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the closed vocabulary is in the schema the model receives
Before: 1 of 2 closed-set string parameters on the Lanes layer published without its enum (set_filter.state has STATE_FILTERS; search_invoices.state has it; area does not)
After: predicted 0 (not built: lib/manifest.ts belongs to ledgerbox-domain-lib)
Method: probe - parameters counted in lib/manifest.ts against the handler's closed list; the file is outside this round's paths
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The legend's swatches misstate the heat of 27 of the 67 marks two chips light
body:
## Summary
The footer legend paints "Late" in the alert colour with the "!" glyph and "Part paid" in the risk colour, but on the seed 17 of 54 late marks are risk and 29 carry no "!", and 10 of 13 part-paid marks are alert.

## Description
components/lanes/model/legend.ts:42 gives `overdue` `heat: "alert", glyph: "!"` and `:45` gives `partial` `heat: "risk"`. The header promises "the colour is the Heat that state reads as on the sheet, and the glyph is one of the three flagOf already draws". But `heatOf` (lib/lanes/heat.ts) makes 1-30 days late `risk` and over 30 `alert`, and `flagOf` (components/lanes/swarm/marks.ts:36) draws "!" only from SHOUT_AT (45) days. A state that spans two heats has no single true swatch, so the key teaches a colour a third of its members do not wear. Fixing it is a design call - two swatches per chip, a neutral swatch for spanning states, or the dominant heat with a note - and it must be seen in the window.

## Flow
- person reads the footer: "Late" chip, red swatch, "!" -> presses it -> 54 marks light, 17 of them amber and 29 with no "!"
- "Part paid" chip, amber swatch -> 13 marks light, 10 of them red
- proposal: decide the encoding for a state spanning heats; change LEGEND's heat/glyph fields; check in the real window, both themes

## Expected impact
The key would match what it lights; measured as swatch-heat mismatches among lit marks (27 of 67 today). Could break: the legend's chip chrome in Foot.tsx if a chip gains a second swatch.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a legend swatch is the colour of the marks its press lights
Before: probe on the seed: overdue by heat { alert: 37, risk: 17 }, 25 of 54 at 45+ days (carry "!"); partial by heat { alert: 10, risk: 3 }
After: unmeasurable until the encoding is chosen
Method: probe - Before counted from buildSheet(); After needs a design decision and the rendered footer
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: 'Long overdue' means over 30 days on the card and 45+ days on its glyph
body:
## Summary
`HEAT_LABEL.alert` says "long overdue" from 31 days (and for any dispute), while the standing glyph's word for long overdue is "45+ days late"; 14 seeded cards print "long overdue" above a glyph whose accessible name says "late" or "a credit is waiting".

## Description
lib/lanes/heat.ts `heatOf` returns `alert` for `daysOverdue > 30` and for `disputed`; HEAT_LABEL.alert is "long overdue", printed as the card's state line (components/lanes/card/Head.tsx:41), in the swarm tip, the foot, and as `heat` in every invoice the agent reads (components/lanes/tools/read.ts:27). The standing (components/lanes/model/status.ts:72) calls an invoice `long-overdue` only from SHOUT_AT = 45, labelled "45+ days late" (STATUS_LABEL), and the footer key publishes "45+ days" as the contract (status.ts:27). One phrase, two thresholds. A disputed invoice inside its terms would also read "long overdue" (none on the seed: both disputes are 54 and 72 days late). Fixed looks like one meaning per word: either the heat word names what alert is ("needs you now", covering disputes) or the threshold moves - a copy and design decision for the owner.

## Flow
- an invoice 35 days late: card head "long overdue"; corner glyph label "late"; read_view gives heat "long overdue", days_overdue 35
- the footer key says "!" = 45+ days; the reader is told twice, differently
- proposal: choose the alert word; change HEAT_LABEL in lib/lanes/heat.ts (the one table since 9e573d2)

## Expected impact
Card, tip, foot and agent read stop disagreeing about what "long overdue" means; measured as cards whose heat word and standing disagree (14 today). Could break: copy on four surfaces and the agent's `heat` field.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - one name, one meaning across the card and its glyph
Before: probe on the seed: 37 marks labelled "long overdue", 14 of them below SHOUT_AT (standing "late" or "credit")
After: unmeasurable until the word is chosen
Method: probe - Before counted from buildSheet(); the After is a copy decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction

title: A read straight after a write answers from the books as they were before it
body:
## Summary
Every BooksTools read answers from the `books` and `sheet` props, and a write only calls `router.refresh()` without waiting, so an agent's next read can describe the books before its own write.

## Description
`settle` (examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/tools/BooksTools.tsx, `router.refresh()`) fires a server re-render and returns the act's answer at once. The read handlers (`read_inbox`, `read_credits`, `read_invoice`, `read_books`, `read_clients`) close over `books` from the last render (`useWebMCPTool` reads the handler through a ref, so the closure is the latest RENDERED one). Until Next re-renders the route, `read_credits` still lists the credit just applied and `read_invoice` the old balance; an agent that re-reads to confirm a match sees it not applied and may apply it again (matchAction then refuses "already applied elsewhere" - safe, but a confusing loop) or report a stale balance. mcp-tools/write-freshness-gate covers the shape ("deciding whether a write result may license skipping the readback"). Fixed looks like: either the write's answer carries the post-write facts the next read would fetch, or reads wait for the refresh that follows a write. Seeing the window between refresh and re-render needs the browser.

## Flow
- agent: match_bank_line(inv, bl) -> matchAction commits -> settle: toast, router.refresh() (not awaited) -> answer "Applied $X to LB-..."
- agent immediately: read_credits() -> handler reads books.credits from the previous render -> bl still listed as unapplied
- proposal: measure the gap with a browser-driven journey (call, read within N ms); then return post-write facts or gate reads on a refresh generation

## Expected impact
An agent's confirm-read after a write agrees with the write; measured as stale reads in a scripted call-then-read journey. Could break: answer shapes of the acts if they grow post-write facts.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a read after a write reflects the write
Before: unmeasured: no harness here renders Next; by reading, every read handler closes over props and settle does not await the refresh
After: unmeasurable without a browser
Method: simulation - the props-closure path walked in BooksTools.tsx; the refresh/re-render window is only observable in the running app
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
